title: A week of real players on my AI game: half the visitors never pressed Play, and my headline stat was a logging bug
author: br1ckface
selftext:
Last week I launched Overswing, a free browser grapple-hook time attack built with Claude Code and Gemini. As my first game, here is what a week of real player data taught me:

**Play free:** [https://br1ckface.itch.io/overswing](https://br1ckface.itch.io/overswing)

https://i.redd.it/r3huyvdjx0vh1.gif

* Itch: 101 page views, 47 plays.
* Server Data: 23 finished a run, 9 completed two runs on their first visit, and 1 returned on a later day.
* One player spent 42 minutes, restarted 164 times, and sent a detailed bug report (wall hits flung players backward, which is now fixed).

The Data "Bug" I initially thought most players quit on the finish screen because the data showed a 75% drop-off. To double-check, I had Claude Code run three research agents alongside a fourth "skeptic" agent meant to challenge their assumptions.

The skeptic spotted the real issue: a logging bug. Restarts were saved locally and sent only on completion or menu return. If someone restarted five times and closed the tab, they looked like a finish-screen drop-off. Plus, anyone leaving during loading went completely untracked. Patch 0.1.12 now fixes this.

Key Lessons

1. Assign a skeptic agent: The analysis improved once an agent audited the logging code.
2. Fact-check AI ideas: An agent suggested rendering hundreds of opponents on screen
3. Track pre-game conversion: I spent time polishing the end screen while half my visitors never even started.

Next up: further updates and optimizations.

If you try it, let me know where you stopped and why! Drop a quick comment with your feedback.
